## A. Algorithm Enhancement Analysis

### A.1 POST-01: Log Transform (xpe_enhance_basic.dll, SWU-2.1)

**Current**: Epsilon floor + monotonic logarithmic transform.

**State-of-the-Art Improvements**:

| Enhancement | Description | Quantitative Target | Reference |
|------------|-------------|-------------------|-----------|
| Adaptive base selection | Log base selected per body part and kVp to optimize dynamic range compression | PSNR improvement >= 2 dB over fixed-base | Standard radiographic practice |
| Segmented log transform | Different log curves for body vs collimated regions using collimation ROI | Eliminate burned-out edges in non-collimated regions | Clinical workflow optimization |
| Reversible precision | IEEE 754 double precision intermediate with guaranteed inverse fidelity | Inverse error < 0.5 ADU over full 16-bit range | Numerical analysis |
| Lookup table acceleration | Pre-computed 65536-entry LUT for uint16 input, interpolated LUT for float32 | < 5ms for 3072x3072 (current budget: 35ms) | Implementation optimization |

**Sub-Functions**:
- `log_compute_base()`: Adaptive base selection from exam profile
- `log_apply_forward()`: Forward transform with epsilon floor
- `log_apply_inverse()`: Inverse with precision guarantee
- `log_build_lut()`: LUT pre-computation for integer paths

---

### A.2 POST-02: Noise Reduction (xpe_enhance_basic.dll, SWU-2.2)

**Current**: Bilateral filter / NLM or wavelet denoising.

**State-of-the-Art Improvements**:

| Enhancement | Description | Quantitative Target | Reference |
|------------|-------------|-------------------|-----------|
| BM3D (Block Matching 3D) | Collaborative filtering via 3D transform-domain shrinkage | PSNR +1.5-3 dB over bilateral | Dabov et al. 2007 (foundational) |
| Guided image filtering | Edge-preserving filter using original image as guide post-enhancement | MTF preservation >= 98% at Nyquist/2 | He et al. 2013 |
| Noise-level adaptive switching | Auto-select bilateral vs NLM vs wavelet based on estimated sigma | Optimal PSNR for each noise regime | [Eulig et al. 2024](https://aapm.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/mp.17379) |
| Dose-aware strength mapping | Noise reduction strength inversely proportional to local mAs/dose | No over-smoothing in well-exposed regions | [Fujifilm FNC approach](https://www.fujifilm.com/products/medical/technologies/fnc/) |
| DL denoiser (Phase 3 fallback) | DnCNN / RED-CNN as premium path | SSIM >= 0.98 (benchmarked vs RED-CNN) | [Springer 2024](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s12530-024-09620-6) |
| Frequency-selective denoising | Wavelet domain: aggressive denoising on HF, preserve LF structure | NPS shape preservation within 10% | Wavelet shrinkage literature |

**Critical Research Finding**: [Benchmarking study (2024)](https://aapm.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/mp.17379) showed RED-CNN (one of the earliest DL methods) still matches newer architectures when evaluated on standardized metrics. No consistent advantage from newer methods -- this validates our pragmatic DnCNN/RED-CNN selection for Phase 3.

**Sub-Functions**:
- `noise_estimate_sigma()`: Wavelet-based sigma estimator (already in API: `xpe_noise_estimate_sigma`)
- `noise_select_method()`: Auto-selection logic based on sigma, body part, dose
- `noise_bilateral_core()`: Bilateral filter kernel with SIMD (AVX2)
- `noise_nlm_core()`: Non-local means with patch preselection
- `noise_wavelet_core()`: DWT-based shrinkage (soft/hard threshold)
- `noise_guided_filter()`: Post-processing edge-aware refinement
- `noise_blend_output()`: Weighted blending for smooth transition zones

---

### A.3 POST-03: Contrast Enhancement (xpe_enhance_basic.dll, SWU-2.3)

**Current**: CLAHE or exam-profile curve with bounded clip limit.

**State-of-the-Art Improvements**:

| Enhancement | Description | Quantitative Target | Reference |
|------------|-------------|-------------------|-----------|
| Multiscale CLAHE | CLAHE applied per Laplacian pyramid level with level-specific clip limits | Contrast improvement >= 30% (CNR metric) without noise amplification | [arXiv:2411.01373](https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.01373) |
| Body-part-adaptive clip limit | Clip limit derived from body part + kVp + mAs profile | Eliminate over-enhancement on low-dose extremities | Clinical profile database |
| Histogram specification | Target histogram shape derived from "ideal" exam exemplar | Consistent visual appearance across dose levels | Histogram matching theory |
| Local tone mapping | Sigmoid-based local contrast with adaptive gain per tile | No halo artifacts at tissue boundaries | [Hindawi 2013](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3876670/) |
| Anti-artifact guard | Overshoot detection on CLAHE output with automatic clip reduction | Zero visible block artifacts | Implementation guardrail |

**Sub-Functions**:
- `contrast_compute_histogram()`: Per-tile histogram computation (parallelizable)
- `contrast_clip_redistribute()`: CLAHE clip limit and redistribution
- `contrast_interpolate_tiles()`: Bilinear interpolation between tile boundaries
- `contrast_profile_select()`: Body-part/dose-based parameter selection
- `contrast_apply_sigmoid()`: Sigmoid tone curve application
- `contrast_artifact_detect()`: Block artifact and halo detection

---

### A.4 POST-04: Edge Enhancement (xpe_enhance_basic.dll, SWU-2.4)

**Current**: Unsharp masking (USM) with overshoot limiter.

**State-of-the-Art Improvements**:

| Enhancement | Description | Quantitative Target | Reference |
|------------|-------------|-------------------|-----------|
| Multi-band USM | Separate sharpening per frequency band (Laplacian pyramid) | MTF boost >= 20% at target frequencies without Nyquist overshoot | Multiresolution processing literature |
| Adaptive radius | USM kernel radius adapted to body part (large for chest, small for extremity) | Clinically optimal sharpness per exam type | Exam profile adaptation |
| Phase-preserving sharpening | Monogenic signal framework for edge enhancement without ringing | Zero visible ringing artifacts at bone-soft tissue boundaries | Felsberg & Sommer (monogenic signal) |
| Directional sharpening | Steerable filters for orientation-selective enhancement | Enhanced trabecular detail without noise amplification | Freeman & Adelson (steerable filters) |
| Overshoot prevention v2 | Percentile-based overshoot clamping (P1/P99 of gradient magnitude) | Overshoot < 2% of local dynamic range | Improved over current limiter |

**Sub-Functions**:
- `edge_compute_unsharp()`: Multi-scale Gaussian subtraction
- `edge_apply_gain()`: Per-band gain application
- `edge_overshoot_clamp()`: Percentile-based overshoot prevention
- `edge_directional_filter()`: Steerable filter computation
- `edge_blend_output()`: Weighted combination of enhanced bands

---

### A.5 POST-05: Multiscale Processing (xpe_enhance_advanced.dll, SWU-2.5)

**Current**: Low-contrast enhancement via frequency decomposition.

**State-of-the-Art Improvements**:

| Enhancement | Description | Quantitative Target | Reference |
|------------|-------------|-------------------|-----------|
| Laplacian pyramid (6-8 levels) | Full Laplacian decomposition with per-level gain/offset control | Visible low-contrast structures enhanced by >= 40% | [Agfa MUSICA approach](https://agfaradiologysolutions.com/products/musica-software/) |
| Nonlinear gain mapping | Sigmoid-shaped gain per decomposition level to prevent saturation | No clipping in any frequency band | MUSICA-class processing |
| Anatomy-aware coefficients | Per-band coefficients indexed by body part and clinical task | Task-specific optimization (e.g., lung nodule visibility) | [PMC8933435](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8933435/) |
| Noise-dependent band suppression | Suppress enhancement in bands dominated by noise (sigma-based gate) | No noise amplification in HF bands for low-dose images | Noise-aware multiscale |
| Edge-preserving reconstruction | Guided filter on reconstruction to prevent band-aliasing artifacts | Zero staircase/halo artifacts | He et al. guided filter |

---

### A.6 POST-07: Collimation Detection (xpe_enhance_advanced.dll, SWU-2.8)

**Current**: Gradient + Hough baseline, AI refinement.

**State-of-the-Art Improvements**:

| Enhancement | Description | Quantitative Target | Reference |
|------------|-------------|-------------------|-----------|
| Canny + Hough robust pipeline | Multi-scale Canny edge detection + probabilistic Hough for line segments | Boundary detection accuracy >= 95% on rectangular collimation | Standard computer vision |
| Circular/polygonal collimation | Extend beyond rectangular to circular (cone beam) and irregular collimation | Support for >= 4 collimation geometries | Clinical variability |
| Confidence scoring | Per-edge confidence based on gradient magnitude and continuity | Low-confidence edges trigger whole-image fallback | Safety: SRS-SAFE-015 |
| Shadow detection | Distinguish collimation edge from anatomy edge using intensity profile analysis | False positive rate < 1% | Histogram-based classification |
| Sub-pixel refinement | Parabolic interpolation on gradient magnitude for sub-pixel boundary | Boundary precision < 0.5 pixel | Sub-pixel edge detection theory |

---

### A.7 POST-06: Body Part Recognition (xpe_ai.dll, SWU-2.7)

**Current**: MobileNet-v3 for 15+ category classification.

**State-of-the-Art Improvements**:

| Enhancement | Description | Quantitative Target | Reference |
|------------|-------------|-------------------|-----------|
| EfficientNet-B0/B1 | Better accuracy/efficiency tradeoff than MobileNet-v3 for medical imaging | Top-1 >= 97% (vs 95% MobileNet-v3) | [ResearchGate comparison](https://www.researchgate.net/publication/381342079_Bone_Fracture_Detection_with_X-Ray_images_using_MobileNet_V3_Architecture) |
| ConvNeXt-Tiny | Modern architecture with better feature extraction for medical images | Top-1 >= 98% with negligible latency increase | [arXiv:2508.11532](https://arxiv.org/html/2508.11532v1) |
| Multi-label classification | Support for multi-region images (e.g., "CHEST+ABDOMEN") | Multi-label F1 >= 0.93 | Clinical workflow |
| Orientation detection | Concurrent AP/PA/lateral detection alongside body part | Orientation accuracy >= 99% | Exam metadata validation |
| Rejection class | "UNKNOWN" class for non-diagnostic images (test patterns, QC images) | False acceptance rate < 0.1% | Safety gate |
| Knowledge distillation | Distill larger teacher model into MobileNet-v3 for deployment | Maintain 97%+ accuracy at MobileNet-v3 latency | Model compression |

---

### A.8 POST-08: Image Stitching (xpe_ai.dll, SWU-2.9)

**Current**: Phase correlation + AI alignment.

**State-of-the-Art Improvements**:

| Enhancement | Description | Quantitative Target | Reference |
|------------|-------------|-------------------|-----------|
| SX-Stitch framework | VMS-UNet segmentation + registration energy minimization | Sub-pixel alignment accuracy | [arXiv:2409.05681](https://arxiv.org/html/2409.05681v1) |
| Feature-based registration | SIFT/ORB features for overlap detection + RANSAC for robust matching | Registration error < 1 pixel | Standard image registration |
| Seam blending | Multi-band blending with Laplacian pyramid at stitch boundary | No visible seam in stitched image | Burt & Adelson pyramid blending |
| Exposure normalization | Per-segment histogram matching before blending | Uniform brightness across segments | Radiometric normalization |
| Motion artifact compensation | Breathing/movement detection and correction between exposures | Artifact-free stitching for thoraco-lumbar images | Motion-aware registration |
| Progressive stitching | Support for 2-5 segment stitching with incremental registration | < 300ms per additional segment | Incremental registration |

---

### A.9 POST-09: Bone Suppression (xpe_ai.dll, SWU-2.11)

**Current**: Residual U-Net.

**State-of-the-Art Improvements**:

| Enhancement | Description | Quantitative Target | Reference |
|------------|-------------|-------------------|-----------|
| xU-NetFullSharp | Novel architecture for bone shadow suppression with attention mechanisms | PSNR >= 35 dB, SSIM >= 0.97 | [ScienceDirect 2024](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S1746809424010413) |
| GAN-based approach | Bone Edge-Guided GAN for sharper soft tissue images | Improved edge preservation vs standard U-Net | [Springer 2020](https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/978-3-030-59713-9_65) |
| Cascade model | Two-stage: bone segmentation + tissue generation | Better generalization to pediatric chest | [ScienceDirect 2022](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0169260722000128) |
| DES-free training | Train on single-energy CXR using CT-derived pseudo-DES pairs | Eliminate need for dual-energy acquisition training data | [PMC9793471](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9793471/) |
| Confidence map output | Per-pixel confidence for suppression quality assessment | Flag regions with suppression uncertainty > 20% | Quality assurance |
| Multi-anatomy support | Extend beyond chest to spine, pelvis, extremities | Top-3 body region support in Phase 3+ | Clinical expansion |

## B. Sub-Module Decomposition

### B.1 xpe_enhance_basic.dll (7 API functions, 5 SWU)

```
xpe_enhance_basic.dll
  |
  +-- SWU-2.1: LogTransform
  |     +-- log_compute_base(bodyPart, kVp) -> base
  |     +-- log_build_lut(base, epsilon, bitDepth) -> LUT[65536]
  |     +-- log_apply_forward_lut(img, lut) -> img'        [SIMD: AVX2 vectorizable]
  |     +-- log_apply_forward_float(img, base, epsilon) -> img'
  |     +-- log_apply_inverse_lut(img, lut) -> img'        [SIMD: AVX2 vectorizable]
  |     +-- log_validate_monotonic(img') -> bool           [Testable independently]
  |
  +-- SWU-2.2: NoiseReducer
  |     +-- noise_estimate_sigma(img) -> sigma              [Already separate API]
  |     +-- noise_select_method(sigma, bodyPart, config) -> method_id
  |     +-- noise_bilateral_core(img, sigma_s, sigma_r) -> img'  [SIMD: parallelizable per row]
  |     +-- noise_nlm_core(img, h, templateSize, searchSize) -> img'  [GPU candidate]
  |     +-- noise_wavelet_shrink(img, levels, threshold_type) -> img'
  |     +-- noise_guided_postfilter(img', guide_img) -> img''
  |     +-- noise_strength_map(sigma_local, mAs, bodyPart) -> strength_map
  |
  +-- SWU-2.3: ContrastEnhancer
  |     +-- contrast_compute_tile_histograms(img, tileW, tileH) -> histograms[]  [Parallel]
  |     +-- contrast_clip_redistribute(histograms[], clipLimit) -> clipped_hists[]
  |     +-- contrast_compute_cdf(clipped_hists[]) -> CDFs[]
  |     +-- contrast_interpolate_tiles(img, CDFs[], tileW, tileH) -> img'
  |     +-- contrast_profile_select(bodyPart, kVp, mAs) -> {clipLimit, tileSize}
  |     +-- contrast_apply_sigmoid(img, center, width, gamma) -> img'  [Alternative to CLAHE]
  |     +-- contrast_artifact_check(img', img) -> artifact_score
  |
  +-- SWU-2.4: EdgeEnhancer
  |     +-- edge_compute_gaussian_pyramid(img, levels) -> pyramid[]  [Reuse from multiscale]
  |     +-- edge_compute_unsharp_mask(img, sigma, amount) -> detail
  |     +-- edge_apply_gain_per_band(details[], gains[]) -> enhanced
  |     +-- edge_overshoot_clamp(enhanced, percentile_lo, percentile_hi) -> clamped
  |     +-- edge_profile_select(bodyPart) -> {sigma, amount, gains[]}
  |
  +-- SWU-2.10: ExposureIndexCalc (Phase 1b baseline)
        +-- ei_select_eit(bodyPart, examView) -> EIT_value
        +-- ei_compute_roi_statistics(img, roi_or_null) -> {mean, median, histogram}
        +-- ei_calc_exposure_index(statistics) -> EI
        +-- ei_calc_deviation_index(EI, EIT) -> DI
        +-- ei_validate_input(img, meta) -> is_valid  [Reject stitched/multi-irradiation]
```

**Data Flow (SWU-2.1 through SWU-2.4)**:
```
float32 img -> [Log Transform] -> log_img -> [Noise Reduce] -> clean_img
  -> [Contrast Enhance] -> contrast_img -> [Edge Enhance] -> enhanced_img
```

**Parallelizable Sub-Functions**:
- `contrast_compute_tile_histograms`: Independent per tile
- `noise_bilateral_core`: Independent per row (with kernel boundary handling)
- `log_apply_forward_lut`: Fully SIMD vectorizable (AVX2 8-wide float)
- `ei_compute_roi_statistics`: Histogram accumulation parallelizable

### B.2 xpe_enhance_advanced.dll (4 API functions, 3 SWU)

```
xpe_enhance_advanced.dll
  |
  +-- SWU-2.5: MultiscaleProcessor
  |     +-- ms_decompose_laplacian(img, levels) -> {pyramid[], residual}  [6-8 levels]
  |     +-- ms_compute_gains(bodyPart, task, noise_sigma) -> gains_per_level[]
  |     +-- ms_apply_nonlinear_gain(pyramid[], gains[]) -> modified_pyramid[]
  |     +-- ms_reconstruct(modified_pyramid[], residual) -> img'
  |     +-- ms_noise_gate(band, sigma_band) -> gated_band      [Per-level noise suppression]
  |     +-- ms_artifact_monitor(img', img) -> artifact_metrics  [Auto-disable trigger]
  |
  +-- SWU-2.6: FractionalProcessor
  |     +-- frac_compute_mask(img) -> frequency_mask   [Grumwald-Letnikov or Caputo]
  |     +-- frac_apply_operator(img, order, mask) -> img'
  |     +-- frac_edge_preserve(img', order) -> img''   [Edge-aware fractional differentiation]
  |     +-- frac_validate_order(order) -> clamped_order  [0.0-2.0 range enforcement]
  |
  +-- SWU-2.8: CollimationDetector
        +-- collim_preprocess(img) -> gradient_magnitude, gradient_direction
        +-- collim_detect_edges_canny(gradient_mag, gradient_dir, thresholds) -> edge_map
        +-- collim_hough_lines(edge_map) -> line_segments[]
        +-- collim_fit_rectangle(line_segments[]) -> {x0, y0, x1, y1, confidence}
        +-- collim_fit_circle(line_segments[]) -> {cx, cy, r, confidence}  [Future]
        +-- collim_score_confidence(roi, img) -> confidence_float
        +-- collim_subpixel_refine(roi, gradient_mag) -> refined_roi
```

### B.3 xpe_display.dll (11 API functions, 4 SWU)

```
xpe_display.dll
  |
  +-- SWU-3.1: ModalityLUT
  |     +-- mlut_apply_linear(img, slope, intercept) -> img'   [SIMD: trivial vectorize]
  |     +-- mlut_apply_sequence(img, lut_data[], lut_len) -> img'  [LUT sequence support]
  |     +-- mlut_validate_params(slope, intercept) -> is_valid
  |
  +-- SWU-3.2: VoiLUT
  |     +-- voi_apply_linear(img, center, width) -> img'       [SIMD]
  |     +-- voi_apply_linear_exact(img, center, width) -> img' [DICOM PS 3.3 exact]
  |     +-- voi_apply_sigmoid(img, center, width) -> img'      [Sigmoid function]
  |     +-- voi_build_8bit_lut(center, width, function) -> lut[65536]  [Pre-compute]
  |     +-- voi_apply_fast_lut(img, lut) -> img_8bit           [Real-time display path]
  |     +-- voi_apply_batch(imgs[], count, center, width) -> imgs'[]
  |     +-- voi_auto_window(img, percentile_lo, percentile_hi) -> {center, width}
  |
  +-- SWU-3.3: PresentationLUT
  |     +-- plut_apply_gsdf(img, target_luminance_range) -> img'
  |     +-- plut_apply_gamma(img, gamma) -> img'
  |     +-- plut_apply_named_preset(img, preset_name) -> img'
  |     +-- plut_check_display_gsdf() -> compliance_score      [GSDF measurement]
  |     +-- plut_build_gsdf_lut(Lmin, Lmax, jnd_count) -> lut[]
  |     +-- plut_format_convert_float_to_uint16(img_float) -> img_uint16  [Final conversion]
  |
  +-- SWU-3.4: LUTManager
        +-- lut_load_builtin_presets() -> preset_count
        +-- lut_load_custom_presets(store_path) -> custom_count
        +-- lut_get_by_index(index) -> {name, description, params}
        +-- lut_add_custom(name, desc, definition_json) -> success
        +-- lut_remove_custom(name) -> success
        +-- lut_auto_select(bodyPart, modality) -> preset_name
        +-- lut_export_json(preset_name) -> json_string
```

### B.5 xpe_ai.dll (7 API functions, 4 SWU)

### B.6 gsvg.dll (8 API functions, 4 SI)

```
gsvg.dll
  |
  +-- SI-001: GridDetector
  |     +-- gdet_compute_fft_2d(pixels, width, height) -> spectrum
  |     +-- gdet_find_peaks(spectrum, pixel_pitch) -> peak_candidates[]
  |     +-- gdet_classify_peaks(candidates[]) -> {freq_lp_mm, angle_deg, confidence}
  |     +-- gdet_validate_detection(freq, angle) -> is_plausible

## C. Enhancement Pipeline Innovation

### C.1 Adaptive Parameter Selection System

**Architecture**: Three-tier parameter selection system driven by (1) exam profile, (2) image statistics, and (3) AI body part classification.

```
Tier 1: Exam Profile (Static)
  Input: bodyPart + examView from DICOM metadata or MWL
  Output: Base parameter set {noise_strength, clahe_clip, edge_amount, ...}
  Source: JSON profile database (e.g., profiles/CHEST_PA.json)

Tier 2: Image Statistics (Dynamic)
  Input: Image statistics {mean, sigma, histogram_shape, SNR_estimate}
  Output: Parameter adjustments {noise_strength_mult, clahe_clip_adj, ...}
  Logic:
    - Low SNR (sigma > threshold): increase noise reduction, decrease edge
    - High dynamic range: reduce CLAHE clip, increase log base
    - Under-exposed (mean < target): boost contrast, reduce noise threshold

Tier 3: AI Refinement (Phase 3)
  Input: Body part classification + confidence
  Output: Fine-tuned parameters for sub-regions
  Logic:
    - CHEST detected: optimize for mediastinum + lung field separately
    - HAND detected: aggressive edge enhancement for trabecular detail
    - SPINE detected: maximize soft tissue contrast in vertebral bodies
```

**Parameter Flow Table**:

| Parameter | Tier 1 Source | Tier 2 Adjustment | Tier 3 AI Refinement |
|-----------|--------------|-------------------|---------------------|
| `noise_strength` | Body part profile | x (sigma/sigma_ref) | Region-specific multiplier |
| `clahe_clip_limit` | Exam type | Adjust by histogram kurtosis | Anatomy-aware clip map |
| `edge_amount` | Body part | Scale by estimated MTF | Bone vs soft tissue regions |
| `edge_radius` | Resolution profile | None | None |
| `multiscale_gains[0..7]` | Exam/task profile | Noise-gated per level | AI-selected task preset |
| `fractional_order` | Body part | Fine structure metric | None |
| `log_base` | Fixed (10.0) | Adaptive by dynamic range | None |

**Implementation**:
```
config = profile_db.get_base_params(bodyPart, examView);    // Tier 1
stats = compute_image_statistics(img);                       // Analysis
config = adjust_by_statistics(config, stats);                // Tier 2
if (ai_available && bodypart_confidence > 0.9) {
    config = ai_refine_params(config, bodypart_label, img);  // Tier 3
}
```

### C.2 Intelligent Auto-Tuning Based on Image Statistics

| Statistic | Computation | Influenced Parameters |
|-----------|-------------|----------------------|
| **Global mean** | `mean(img[ROI])` | Log base, VOI window center |
| **Global sigma** | `std(img[ROI])` | Noise reduction strength, edge amount |
| **Noise sigma** | Wavelet-based (MAD estimator on HH subband) | Noise method selection, denoising strength |
| **Histogram entropy** | `-sum(p*log(p))` | CLAHE clip limit, contrast mode |
| **Dynamic range ratio** | `(P99 - P1) / max_possible` | Log transform parameters |
| **Local contrast index** | Mean of local std / local mean per 64x64 block | Multiscale gains, edge enhancement |
| **Edge density** | Fraction of pixels with gradient > threshold | Edge enhancement amount |
| **SNR estimate** | `mean(signal_region) / sigma(background_region)` | Overall processing aggressiveness |

**Auto-Tuning Decision Table**:

| Condition | Action |
|-----------|--------|
| SNR < 10 | Switch noise reduction to NLM, reduce edge to 50%, suppress HF multiscale bands |
| SNR 10-30 | Standard bilateral, normal edge, standard multiscale |
| SNR > 30 | Minimal noise reduction, aggressive edge, full multiscale |
| Entropy < 4.0 (low contrast) | Increase CLAHE clip 2x, boost mid-frequency multiscale gains |
| Entropy > 7.0 (high detail) | Reduce CLAHE clip 0.5x, preserve existing contrast structure |
| Dynamic range < 50% | Apply histogram stretching before CLAHE |
| Under-exposure (DI < -3) | Alert + aggressive contrast boost + noise reduction priority |

---

### C.3 Multi-Resolution Processing Framework

**Architecture**: Unified Laplacian pyramid shared across noise reduction, contrast enhancement, edge enhancement, and multiscale processing.

```
Input float32 image
    |
    v
[Laplacian Pyramid Decomposition] (8 levels)
    |
    +-> Level 0 (finest): Edge enhancement domain
    +-> Level 1-2 (fine): Noise reduction domain (HF noise)
    +-> Level 3-5 (medium): Contrast enhancement domain
    +-> Level 6-7 (coarse): Structure / anatomy domain
    +-> Residual (DC): Overall brightness / exposure
    |
[Per-Level Processing]
    Level 0-1: Wavelet shrinkage (noise) + gain (edge)
    Level 2-4: CLAHE-equivalent per-level histogram processing
    Level 5-7: Anatomy-aware gain (multiscale processing)
    Residual:  Global brightness normalization
    |
[Reconstruction]
    |
    v
Output enhanced image
```

**Advantages**:
- Single decomposition shared across 4 processing stages (saves 3x computation)
- No inter-stage artifact accumulation (all processing in decomposition domain)
- Natural frequency-domain noise gating (noise only in high-frequency bands)
- Unified parameter model: one gain vector per level controls all processing

**Performance Estimate**: Combined multi-resolution processing < 250ms for 3072x3072 (vs current sequential chain: 170 + 120 + 80 = 370ms).

---

### C.4 Frequency-Domain Processing Alternatives

| Current Approach | Frequency Alternative | Advantage | Complexity |
|-----------------|----------------------|-----------|------------|
| Bilateral filter (spatial) | Guided filter in Laplacian domain | 3-5x faster, same quality | Medium |
| CLAHE (tile-based) | Per-band histogram equalization | No tile boundary artifacts | Low |
| USM (spatial kernel) | Per-band gain in Laplacian domain | Multi-scale sharpening inherent | Low |
| NLM (patch matching) | BM3D (block matching in 3D transform) | Better PSNR for similar compute | High |
| Multiscale (separate pass) | Integrated in shared pyramid | Eliminates redundant decomposition | Low (already proposed) |

**Recommended Hybrid Architecture**:
- Phase 1b: Spatial-domain processing (bilateral, CLAHE, USM) -- simple, reliable, well-understood
- Phase 2: Transition to unified Laplacian pyramid for multiscale + fractional
- Phase 3+: Full frequency-domain pipeline with shared decomposition

## D. GSVG Deep Enhancement

### D.1 State-of-the-Art Grid Suppression Algorithms

| Method | Approach | Performance | Drawback |
|--------|----------|-------------|----------|
| **DWT Notch Filter** (current) | Wavelet decomposition + frequency-selective filtering | Good grid removal, some MTF loss | Fixed bandwidth may affect nearby anatomy frequencies |
| **2D DWT Band-Stop** | Multi-scale DWT with automatic Gaussian band-stop at grid harmonic | [Excellent grid removal, preserves anatomy](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5352826/) | Requires careful bandwidth selection |
| **Sparse Dictionary** | Dictionary learning for grid pattern + sparse coding for separation | [Better texture preservation than frequency methods](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S1746809423006808) | Higher computational cost |
| **Deep CNN Suppression** | End-to-end CNN trained on grid/no-grid pairs | [Potentially superior to hand-crafted filters](https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2020SPIE11313E..27K/abstract) | Requires training data, Phase 3 dependency |
| **Bayesian Approach** | Probabilistic grid model with MAP estimation | [Robust to grid orientation variation](https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/document/8451541/) | Computationally expensive |

**Recommended Enhancement Path**:

1. **Phase 2 (Current)**: DWT-based notch filter with improved adaptive bandwidth selection
2. **Phase 2+**: Add sparse dictionary method as premium option for difficult cases
3. **Phase 3**: Train CNN-based suppressor as AI worker task

### D.2 Virtual Grid Quality Comparison

| Metric | Physical 6:1 Grid | Physical 12:1 Grid | Virtual Grid (Current Target) | Virtual Grid (Enhanced Target) |
|--------|-------------------|--------------------|-----------------------------|-------------------------------|
| **CNR** | Baseline (1.0) | ~1.5x | >= 0.9x (6:1 equivalent) | >= 1.2x (between 6:1 and 12:1) |
| **MTF preservation** | -5% to -10% (grid cutoff) | -8% to -15% | <= -5% MTF loss | <= -3% MTF loss |
| **Scatter reduction** | 60-80% | 80-95% | 50-70% estimated | 70-85% (with DL scatter model) |
| **Dose impact** | +2-3x (Bucky factor) | +3-5x | 0x (no grid = no dose penalty) | 0x |
| **Artifacts** | Grid line artifacts possible | Moire possible | No physical artifacts | No physical artifacts |

**Key Differentiator**: Virtual grid eliminates dose penalty while approaching 6:1 grid quality. Enhanced target with DL scatter estimation could approach 12:1 grid quality.

### D.3 Novel Frequency-Domain Approaches

| Technique | Description | Implementation Complexity |
|-----------|-------------|--------------------------|
| **Harmonic-aware notch** | Detect grid fundamental + 2-3 harmonics, apply narrow notch at each | Medium -- extends current DWT approach |
| **Directional wavelet** | Curvelets or shearlets for direction-selective grid removal | High -- new decomposition required |
| **Multi-orientation support** | Handle grids at arbitrary angles (not just 0/90 degrees) | Medium -- extend Hough detection to arbitrary angle |
| **Spectral subtraction** | Estimate grid-only spectrum from collimation region, subtract from full image | Medium -- requires collimation detection first |

### D.4 Scatter Estimation Neural Networks

| Model | Architecture | Training Data | Performance | Reference |
|-------|-------------|---------------|-------------|-----------|
| **Deep Scatter Estimation (DSE)** | U-Net variant | Monte Carlo simulation pairs | Real-time scatter estimation, matches MC accuracy | [Springer 2018](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s10921-018-0507-z) |
| **ComptoNet** | Dual-network encoder-decoder | Physics-informed Compton scattering model | Decouples primary from scatter with physics prior | Research 2024 |
| **Simurgh + DL** | Combined hardware/software | Real scatter measurements + augmentation | 10x scan time reduction with flaw preservation | [Springer 2025](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s10921-025-01228-3) |

**Recommended for XPE**: DSE-style U-Net trained on Monte Carlo simulated scatter for the specific detector geometry. Deploy as Phase 3 xpe_ai.dll worker task with Phase 2 LUT-based fallback.

**Quantization Workflow**:
```
1. Train model in FP32 (PyTorch/TensorFlow)
2. Export to ONNX (opset 17+)
3. Calibrate INT8 using 100+ representative images
4. Validate: accuracy drop < 1% on golden test set
5. Deploy quantized model to xpe_ai_worker.exe
6. Fallback: FP32 model if INT8 validation fails
```

```

    |
    v
[Worker Process Alive?]

    |
    v
[Send Request via IPC]
    |
    v
[Wait for Response (timeout: configurable, default 3000ms)]

## F. Display Processing Innovation

### F.1 HDR Tone Mapping for X-ray

**Problem**: X-ray images have > 12-bit dynamic range (16,000:1) but displays show 8-10 bit (256-1024:1). Current VOI LUT is a simple linear/sigmoid window that discards information outside the window.

| Technique | Description | Advantage | Implementation |
|-----------|-------------|-----------|---------------|
| **Global tone mapping** | Reinhard-style global operator adapted for X-ray | Preserves full dynamic range in single view | `display_hdr_tonemap_global(img, key_value)` |
| **Local tone mapping** | Durand bilateral decomposition: compress base, preserve detail | Best detail visibility across wide range | `display_hdr_tonemap_local(img, sigma_s, sigma_r, contrast)` |
| **Dual-window display** | Simultaneous display of two VOI windows (e.g., bone + soft tissue) | Clinical workflow for chest reading | GUI-level feature with blended output |
| **Adaptive window** | Auto-select window from image statistics and body part | Consistent initial presentation | Already planned (`xpe_lut_auto_select`) |
| **Multi-exposure fusion** | Mertens exposure fusion on multiple virtual "exposures" | Maximum detail across full range | `display_hdr_mertens(img, weights[])` |

### F.2 Perceptual-Based Window/Level Optimization

| Feature | Current | Enhanced |
|---------|---------|----------|
| **Auto-window** | Based on histogram percentiles | Perceptual contrast maximization (Weber contrast model) |
| **Tissue-specific** | Single window for entire image | Separate optimal windows for lung / mediastinum / bone |
| **Dose-adaptive** | Fixed algorithm | Wider window for low-dose (accommodate higher noise) |
| **Display-adaptive** | GSDF-based | Ambient light compensation + display characterization |

**Auto-Window Algorithm Enhancement**:
```
1. Compute image histogram within collimation ROI
2. Identify tissue peaks (multi-modal Gaussian mixture)
3. Select window center at dominant tissue peak
4. Set window width to span mean +/- 2*sigma of target tissue
5. Apply GSDF correction for display-specific luminance mapping
6. Adjust for ambient illumination (if sensor available)
```

### F.3 GSDF Compliance Verification

**Current**: `xpe_presentation_lut_check_display()` returns a compliance score.

**Enhanced Verification**:

| Check | Method | Pass Criteria |
|-------|--------|---------------|
| JND linearity | Measure luminance at 18 GSDF reference levels | All JND steps within +/-10% of GSDF target |
| Lmin/Lmax range | Measure display minimum and maximum luminance | Lmin <= 1.0 cd/m2, Lmax >= 350 cd/m2 (diagnostic) |
| Ambient light ratio | Measure ambient illuminance | Ambient < 10% of Lmin for diagnostic displays |
| Uniformity | Measure luminance at 5 points (center + 4 corners) | Uniformity >= 70% (center vs worst corner) |
| Temporal stability | Measure luminance drift over 30 minutes | Drift < 5% from initial measurement |
| Color temperature | Measure white point | Within D65 +/- 500K for grayscale |

|---------|-------------|
| **Runtime GSDF LUT generation** | Build display-specific GSDF correction LUT from measured Lmin/Lmax |
| **Ambient compensation** | Adjust GSDF LUT based on ambient light sensor (if available) |
| **Multi-display support** | Different GSDF LUTs per connected display |
